key_insight: A single integrated framework couples a forward predictive model with an inverse generative model to design liquid electrolyte formulations, and three high-conductivity candidates proposed by the system were experimentally validated.
problem_solved: Accelerates and automates discovery in a vast electrolyte formulation space by enabling design-by-performance (inverse design) rather than costly trial-and-error or one-way prediction.
method: Train a forward predictive model to map electrolyte formulations to target properties (e.g., ionic conductivity).
Develop an inverse generative model conditioned on desired properties to propose new formulations, guided by the forward model.
Close the loop with candidate selection and experimental validation to verify and refine model proposals.
impact: Demonstrates a transferable AI pattern—coupling predictive and generative models with experimental feedback—that reduces experimental workload and speeds materials/formulation discovery, useful across battery, chemistry, and materials ML projects.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing forward predictor → property estimate and inverse generator → proposed formulations with a closed-loop arrow to experiments.
Scatter plot of predicted vs measured conductivity highlighting the three experimentally validated high-conductivity candidates.
Latent-space or conditional generation map illustrating how target properties steer formulation sampling.
Icons: battery/electrolyte vial, neural network/model, lab flask/test tube to represent prediction, generation, and validation steps.
paper_title: A unified predictive and generative solution for liquid electrolyte formulation
paper_authors: Zhenze Yang, Yifan Wu, Xu Han, Ziqing Zhang, Haoen Lai
